buildMethod: All 4 rails (schoolDistrict, utilityService, overlayDistricts, agValuation) fanned to one subagent each in parallel rather than pilot-one-then-scale, each briefed with the CP1 design and live-verified technical constraints. The planner adversarially reviewed every diff (read every source file in full) before this checkpoint; no subagent touched git. Two shared files (src/control/writer-allowlist.mjs, src/cli.mjs) were deliberately withheld from every subagent's scope and wired by the planner afterward to avoid 4-way merge conflicts on the same lines.

adversarialReviewFindings.finding: Inconsistency across subagents: acquire-school-district.mjs called requireWriterJob (gating it behind the parcel_record writer allowlist) while the other 3 acquire scripts (acquire-utility-ccn, acquire-overlay-districts, acquire-ag-valuation) correctly did not, matching the established landing-import.mjs precedent that a cortex-staging job is not a parcel_record writer.
adversarialReviewFindings.resolution: Rather than strip the gate and rewrite acquire-school-district's tests, added it to WRITER_JOBS with an honest kind:"gis-acquire", liveRest:true entry -- more transparent than removing a working, tested check, and liveRest is pure bookkeeping (only requireEasementNoLiveRest's hardcoded easement-only check reads it).

adversarialReviewFindings.finding: test/parcel-overlay-districts.test.mjs contained a test asserting parcel-overlay-districts was NOT on WRITER_JOBS (deliberately written by that subagent to document the pre-wiring gap, with its own comment instructing the planner to flip it).
adversarialReviewFindings.resolution: Flipped to assert presence, per the test's own instruction, after adding the real entry.

notVerifiedThisCheckpointAndWhy.writeJobsAgainstLiveStagingData: None of the 4 write jobs (parcel-school-district, parcel-utility-service, parcel-overlay-districts, parcel-ag-valuation) could be dry-run against real cortex data at this checkpoint: each reads its rail's staging table (tx_school_district, tx_puct_ccn, tx_city_overlay, tx_wcad_ag_valuation) directly in its zone-major hoist SQL, and none of those tables exist yet in the live store -- they are created only by their corresponding acquire job's --apply run, which this session deliberately did not execute (gated behind FACTORY_CLOUD=1, and per the session's own scope decision to stop at ready-to-deploy rather than run --apply itself). Attempting a dry-run now would only produce a 'relation does not exist' Postgres error, not a meaningful validation. This is a structural sequencing fact of the two-layer architecture, not a gap the planner could close from a laptop -- the real validation path is: deploy this card's cloudbuild.parcel-acquire-gis.yaml, execute each acquire job with --apply for at least one county/statewide, THEN dry-run (and eventually --apply) its paired write job.
